prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production 2D Soldier survivor animation for Grave Accord. Image 1 is the approved complete idle strip for this exact facing; it locks identity, camera and equipment grip. Image 2 is the original shipped single-facing seed. Both references show the required direction; do not invent an opposite-facing view. Preserve the same young adult woman Mara Rook, chin-length wavy chestnut hair, dark navy peaked officer cap with a small brass badge/band, ragged long split navy-blue officer coat with restrained brass trim and a sleeve crest, charcoal trousers, brown leather lace-up boots and gloves, utility belt pouches, small brass belt chain and one cross-body strap matching the reference. ONE compact dark brass pistol stays in the physical RIGHT trigger hand with the LEFT hand supporting the grip. Keep the same compact pistol, two arms, face and cap in every pose; no rifle, second pistol, sword, holster swap, new hat, mirrored strap or added ornament. Use restrained dry black ink and matte opaque gouache, broad quiet color planes and selective practical contours. Avoid glossy gradients, excessive tiny scratches, decorative filigree or noise. Maintain two arms, two legs and one intact body/weapon in every pose.
Every pose faces EAST, screen RIGHT, in the exact approved side/three-quarter angle. Nose and both boots point screen RIGHT. Physical RIGHT is the near-side rear trigger arm; LEFT is the forward support arm. Do not exchange grips, turn the chest to face the viewer, or mirror the other facing.
Draw EXACTLY EIGHT full-body poses in a roomy FOUR-column by TWO-row grid, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. One continuous grounded running cycle toward screen RIGHT: 1 forward foot plants while rear heel lifts, 2 weight passes over that support, 3 rear foot swings forward beneath the body, 4 feet exchange with a short light step, 5 opposite foot plants, 6 weight passes over that support, 7 other leg swings forward, 8 return toward frame 1. Alternate the two original legs naturally; no duplicated boots, sliding static legs or unrelated stances. Every head/chest/boot stays in the SAME exact EAST facing throughout. Keep the original two-handed ready weapon hold, cap/hood, physical equipment sides, belt, satchel and short controlled coat movement. The weapon stays rigid and attached to both hands. No shooting, muzzle flash, recoil, roll, fall, airborne leap, particle, effect or ground shadow.
Use ONE shared character scale across all eight poses and one ground baseline per row. Leave at least eight percent of the canvas width clear at its outer left and right edges, and large transparent gutters between COMPLETE bodies, coats and barrels. Each full pose including its entire gun must fit wholly inside its own allotted cell with generous empty space. Draw the figures smaller rather than touching a neighbor or clipping an exterior edge. Genuine RGBA transparency, alpha zero everywhere outside each complete pose, including between limbs. No floor, scenery, background, haze, gradient, border, grid line, label, text or number. Match the approved restrained matte ink/gouache style and original identity.
